title: One change on bin/relay holds every item naming it
what: Measure from git 24-28 Oct how often two branches both changing bin/relay (and other files named by many items) conflicted at take or train; from that, a short fixed list of hub files that the start filter ignores (principle 5: a fact goes to a fixed list), kept in one place the filter and its test read.
why: 28 Oct ~08:45 UTC, right after the start filter fix landed: relay-land took bin/relay, and the next two items in queue order waited ('waits for bin/relay (same file as relay-land...)'); 15 open items name bin/relay in `where`, and relay-land is a 3h feature. bin/relay is the command dispatcher: each item adds or edits its own subcommand, and git merges such edits cleanly almost always. The design for grouping (28 Oct, revision 2) measured that `where` catches 31 % of real overlaps only with such hub files left out; the start filter has no hub list, so a hub serializes the queue. Not measured: how many bin/relay merges conflicted 24-28 Oct.
failing_case: Open items a (where bin/relay, lib/relay_x.py) and b (where bin/relay, lib/relay_y.py), a taken: b waits for bin/relay.
pass_cases: Two items sharing a non-hub file still wait for each other.
The measurement and the hub list's reason are in the item notes.
